steps.say: Antiphospholipid syndrome is an autoimmune thrombophilia characterized by vascular thrombosis, arterial, venous, or microvascular, and/or pregnancy morbidity, occurring as primary APS or secondary to another autoimmune disease, predominantly systemic lupus erythematosus. It is defined by clots in vessels or by losses in placenta.
steps.tx: **Antiphospholipid syndrome** (APS) is an autoimmune **thrombophilia** characterized by **vascular thrombosis** (arterial, venous, or microvascular) and/or **pregnancy morbidity**, occurring as primary APS or secondary to another autoimmune disease (predominantly systemic lupus erythematosus). It is defined by clots in vessels or by losses in placenta.

vis.alt: Body map of arterial, venous and microvascular thrombosis with livedo, Libman-Sacks endocarditis and digital gangrene in APS.
vis.caption: Arterial, venous and microvascular targets with skin, valve and digit signs. Criteria are in the text, not on the drawing (StewardMD).

steps.say: The 2023 ACR EULAR classification criteria for APS employ an entry criterion requiring at least one positive antiphospholipid antibody test within three years of an APS-associated clinical event, evaluated across weighted clinical domains and laboratory domains, requiring at least three points in both clinical and laboratory domains. Entry plus dual triples classify.
steps.tx: The **2023 ACR/EULAR** classification criteria for APS employ an **entry criterion** requiring at least one positive antiphospholipid antibody test within **3 years** of an APS-associated clinical event, evaluated across weighted clinical domains (venous thromboembolism, arterial thrombosis, microvascular domains, obstetric domains) and laboratory domains, requiring **>=3 points** in both clinical and laboratory domains. Entry plus dual triples classify.

rows: Positive antibody within 3 years of event
3 or more points in both domains

steps.say: The classical laboratory criteria antibodies are lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin IgG and IgM, and anti-beta-2-glycoprotein I IgG and IgM. A positive test must be confirmed on two or more occasions at least twelve weeks apart to exclude transient post-infectious antibodies. Persistence proves pathogenicity.
steps.tx: The **classical laboratory criteria antibodies** are **lupus anticoagulant (LA)**, **anticardiolipin (aCL) IgG/IgM**, and **anti-beta-2-glycoprotein I (anti-beta2GPI) IgG/IgM**. A positive test must be confirmed on **two or more occasions** at least **12 weeks apart** to exclude transient post-infectious antibodies. Persistence proves pathogenicity.

rows: Two or more occasions, 12 or more weeks apart

steps.say: The triple-positive antiphospholipid profile denotes simultaneous presence of lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin IgG, and anti-beta-2-glycoprotein I IgG. It is the highest risk phenotype for recurrent arterial and venous thrombosis, pregnancy loss, and progression to catastrophic APS. Three antibodies together are the menace.
steps.tx: The **triple-positive** antiphospholipid profile denotes simultaneous presence of **lupus anticoagulant**, **anticardiolipin IgG**, and **anti-beta-2-glycoprotein I IgG**. It is the highest risk phenotype for recurrent arterial and venous thrombosis, pregnancy loss, and progression to **catastrophic APS**. Three antibodies together are the menace.

vis.alt: Multi-organ microthrombosis in brain, lung, heart, skin, kidney and adrenal with microthrombi and schistocytes in catastrophic APS.
vis.caption: Multi-organ microthrombosis of catastrophic APS, the extreme the triple profile risks. Risk levels are in the text, not on the drawing (StewardMD).

steps.say: Lupus anticoagulant testing follows a mandatory multi-step algorithm: initial screening prolongation of a phospholipid-dependent clotting assay such as dilute Russell viper venom time or sensitive aPTT, failure to correct prolongation upon one-to-one mixing with normal platelet-poor plasma, and definitive correction upon addition of excess confirmatory phospholipids. Prolong, persist, correct.
steps.tx: **Lupus anticoagulant testing** follows a mandatory multi-step algorithm: initial screening prolongation of a **phospholipid-dependent clotting assay** (e.g., **dilute Russell viper venom time [dRVVT]** or sensitive **aPTT**), failure to correct prolongation upon **1:1 mixing** with normal platelet-poor plasma, and definitive **correction** upon addition of excess confirmatory phospholipids. Prolong, persist, correct.

steps.say: First-line secondary antithrombotic prophylaxis for definitive venous thromboembolism in APS is therapeutic anticoagulation with vitamin K antagonists such as warfarin titrated to a target INR of two point zero to three point zero. Randomized controlled trials TRAPS and ASTRO-APS demonstrated that direct oral anticoagulants such as rivaroxaban are inferior and confer excess arterial thrombotic risk in triple-positive APS. Warfarin holds veins; pills fail triples.
steps.tx: First-line secondary antithrombotic prophylaxis for definitive venous thromboembolism in APS is therapeutic anticoagulation with **vitamin K antagonists** (**warfarin**) titrated to a target **INR of 2.0 to 3.0**. Randomized controlled trials (**TRAPS** and **ASTRO-APS**) demonstrated that **direct oral anticoagulants** (**DOACs**, e.g., **rivaroxaban**) are inferior and confer excess arterial thrombotic risk in triple-positive APS. Warfarin holds veins; pills fail triples.

rows: Inferior, excess arterial risk in triple positive (TRAPS, ASTRO-APS)

steps.say: Obstetric APS clinical criteria include three or more unexplained consecutive spontaneous abortions before the tenth week of gestation, one or more unexplained fetal death of a morphologically normal fetus at or beyond the tenth week, or one or more premature birth of a normal neonate before the thirty fourth week due to severe preeclampsia, eclampsia, or placental insufficiency. Three early, one late, and one premature are the bars.
steps.tx: **Obstetric APS** clinical criteria include **>=3 unexplained consecutive spontaneous abortions** before the **10th week** of gestation, **>=1 unexplained fetal death** of a morphologically normal fetus at or beyond the **10th week**, or **>=1 premature birth** of a normal neonate before the **34th week** due to severe **preeclampsia**, eclampsia, or **placental insufficiency**. Three early, one late, and one premature are the bars.

rows: 1 or more normal fetus at or beyond week 10
1 or more before week 34 for preeclampsia or placental failure

steps.say: Standard management of confirmed obstetric APS during pregnancy is combined prophylaxis with low-dose aspirin seventy five to one hundred milligrams daily starting preconception and prophylactic-dose low molecular weight heparin such as enoxaparin forty milligrams daily initiated as soon as intrauterine pregnancy is confirmed, continued throughout gestation and for six weeks postpartum. Dual cover from planning past puerperium.
steps.tx: Standard management of confirmed **obstetric APS** during pregnancy is combined prophylaxis with low-dose **aspirin** (**75 to 100 mg daily**) starting preconception and prophylactic-dose **low molecular weight heparin** (**LMWH**, e.g., **enoxaparin 40 mg daily**) initiated as soon as intrauterine pregnancy is confirmed, continued throughout gestation and for **6 weeks postpartum**. Dual cover from planning past puerperium.

rows: Enoxaparin 40 mg daily from confirmed intrauterine pregnancy
